review_type: Independent read-only TV seek state, integration and native API source review; report-only write
findings: One native request remains in flight; accumulated remote intent is stored separately from decoder position and only the newest queued request survives.
Drag preview issues no native request; release dispatches the latest target, while cancel restores the pre-drag intent and flushes any legitimate queued request.
Native completion during preview does not finalize preview or overwrite its target; bounded four-second settling holds the requested display then returns to actual decoder time.
Manual operations reject invalid duration/target; release, background, episode and quality transitions reset pending input and remove callbacks.
Paused seek retains playWhenReady false; source callback ownership and generation checks retain existing lifecycle and auto-next boundaries.
D-pad up/down can reach the native progress bar and return to the existing action row; left/right on the bar uses 10-second coalesced input instead of native percent steps.
White thumb and filled track remain visible on the inherited dark/focused-blue background; the bar preserves a 48dp target.
Native completion cannot auto-advance while dragging or while a pending earlier seek has priority.
API26 seekTo(long,SEEK_CLOSEST) is isolated behind the version guard; API21 compatibility call and existing API23 speed guard are retained.

official_api_sources.facts: Long/mode overload and SEEK_CLOSEST require API26; legacy int overload uses previous sync frame; closest frame may have larger decoding overhead.

remaining_risks: No TV or emulator validated focus navigation, touch cancellation, actual seek latency, buffering or decoder precision.
Older Android systems retain key-frame-limited positioning; closest-frame mode can require extra decoding and is not a guarantee of faster seeking.
